analysis.title: Global Credit Trader: Taking Stock of Performance and Where to Invest From Here
key_insights: GS review of aggregate data on the largest U.S. corporate credit mutual funds and ETFs finds performance has been challenged over the past few months. It is most visible in HY, which has not benefited as much as IG from the recent rally in rates.
Isolating the largest actively managed funds, performance over the past month has been uniformly challenging across IG and HY versus benchmark returns.

The split between AI and non-AI risk makes correlation an increasingly important consideration for allocators. Industry diversification can help insulate portfolios from further AI-related supply indigestion.

In IG, Utilities, Financials and Healthcare/Pharma have shown lower correlation to AI-related spreads. Energy also stands out in HY. GS views adding these 'defensive' sectors as a prudent risk management tool.
The HY market has traded in three parts: AI-related, performing HY, and distressed. GS is neutral on HY AI-related credit, particularly project finance structures.
In distressed HY, GS remains underweight CCCs because macro and refinancing stresses are unlikely to abate in the near term.
Within performing HY, GS expects BBs to absorb the brunt of future AI-related financing, with potential duration headwinds if rates drift higher. It prefers to own carry in the B-rated cohort.
GS expects dispersion within single-Bs to rise, as there is little room for error on fundamentals.
GS expects compression in non-AI IG and continues to favor BBBs over higher-rated peers.

For crossover investors, GS prefers moving down in capital structure seniority, to capture a subordination spread premium, over moving down in credit quality. Corporate hybrids and U.S. bank subordinated debt both screen as attractive.
EUR credit technicals have so far benefited from less AI-related issuance. Elevated energy prices and, more recently, sovereign and fiscal risks have offset this and pushed spreads wider.
GS prefers USD over EUR credit. It remains underweight French banks but is constructive on the broader European Banks sector.
